text:
Priya: Heads-up: we've got a reproducible perf regression on Mixtral-8x/8 after yesterday's kernel-picker heuristic tweak. p50 unchanged, but p95 +12% and p99 +25% for small chat requests (<=64 tokens). Investigating
Mo: repro steps?
Priya: Quick repro (local machine, dedicated):
```
MODEL=mixtral-8x8
PROMPT_TEMPLATE=\"<BOS> user: {user}
assistant: \"
REQUEST: short chat history, 2 turns, lots of emoji in user turn
```
Tokenization counts vary between 18-26 tokens depending on emoji placement; see below. Baseline (pre-heuristic) p95 78ms, after change p95 87ms.
Devon: interesting — any kernel switch logs?
Priya: yes, grabbed runtime debug:
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:02Z] kernel_picker: initial_kernel=rope-optimized
[2026-03-10T14:12:02Z] tokenizer: mode=UTF8 (byte-fallback=false)
[2026-03-10T14:12:02Z] kernel_picker: switched_kernel=byte-fallback (reason=detected high 2+ byte sequences)
[2026-03-10T14:12:02Z] kv_cache: invalidate_prefix (prefix_len=18 -> 24)
[2026-03-10T14:12:02Z] kernel_picker: final_kernel=byte-fallback
```
Priya: Effect is: kernel selected initially for rope paths, then tokenizer reports a byte-fallback path because of isolated emoji sequences -> we recompile/choose byte kernel and reset kv prefix slots which thrashes the KV cache for that request. That explains the p95+p99 tail.
Mo: so the kernel-picker change made it more optimistic early and then reactive to tokenizer result. Previously we used tokenizer-normalized length before choosing kernel, right?
Priya: right. The tweak tried to pick by architectural hints earlier (heads/kv dims + seq len histogram) to reduce latency for long-lived sessions. But with chat templates that inject BOS/assistant tokens and with emoji-heavy user text, observed tokenization variance causes flip.
Samir: Can we avoid the flip by delaying final kernel selection until after tokenization is done? Or at least avoid invalidating the existing KV layout if change is only length/byte-mode?
Devon: options:
- Delay kernel switch until after tokenization (adds small scheduling cost but prevents KV thrash).
- Use a sticky-kernel policy per-request: first chunk picks kernel, subsequent sub-chunks can only choose fallback if incompatible (and then use fallback without invalidating KV).
- Update tokenizer normalization to pre-normalize chat templates and collapse assistant prefix so token counts are stable.
Priya: I ran a quick microbenchmark: delaying final kernel decision by 1 sync point adds ~1-2ms overhead on p50 but cuts p95 regression by ~70%.
perf-bot: alert created: perf/regression/mixtral-kernel-flip #4227 (linked to this thread)
Mo: let's try 2-step: 1) immediate canary: sticky-kernel per-request (no KV invalidation), 2) follow-up: normalize templates at join-time. Devon can you spin canary?
Devon: will do. I'll add a small harness that fuzzes emoji placement + chat templates and run against both Qwen and Mixtral images. Plan: 100k samples over 30m, measuring kernel_switch_count and kv_invalidate_count.
Samir: also add a metric to tokenization stage: pre_norm_token_count vs post_norm_token_count so we can see how many requests have delta>2.
Priya: created canary config and canary job on dedicated fleet (canary id: mixtral-kernel-fix-20260310). Running now, will post preliminary numbers in ~45m.
Mo: thanks. If canary looks good we should revert the optimistic early-pick in next release or gate it behind dedicated-only flag.
Priya: agree. I'll open the PR with the sticky-kernel fix + metrics and a follow-up issue to improve template normalization.
Samir: nice triage, thanks all :thumbsup:
Priya: quick note for the release notes: root cause = tokenizer-mode/emoji-induced byte-fallback flip triggering kernel reselect + KV prefix invalidation -> tail latency regression. Proposed mitigation = sticky per-request kernel + template normalization.
Devon: tagging @eng-runtime on the PR for review.
Priya: will follow up with the canary numbers when ready.
